### D3 red team · Question

Event: `9ee5f92f54368a215a853ea500c13587` · 2026-09-24T22:49:53Z

> D3 code review 5: ipd, checkpoint (b). Read in the scratch worktree /tmp/d3cr1 at d5b1cd85f, covering scope, args, sizing, stack, fs, server, link, netd and bin line by line. I wrote throwaway attack tests and planted bugs; all were reverted and the tree is clean. Baseline: 43 tests pass.
> 
> VERDICT: OK with notes. There is no path back to the box through connect, and the ISN claim holds. Three P2s should be fixed before merge: an incomplete martian drop, sockets outside the worst-case and fair-share rules, and test gaps on the ingress badge.
> 
> == Paths back to the box ==
> - **connect:** the self set is checked, then the scope, then state, then link, then an ephemeral port, then a fresh interface, before smoltcp sees anything (stack.rs connect). The self set is own address, network and broadcast, 255.255.255.255, 127/8, 0/8, 224/4, 240/4 and every self=. Args refuse len 0, 31 and 32, an addr that is the network or broadcast address, and a gateway off the network.
> - **smoltcp internals:** a fragment can't be used to reach a listener through the main interface. I tested a SYN with MF set: smoltcp's Ipv4Repr::parse refuses fragments when the fragmentation feature is off (wire/ipv4.rs:557), so it is dropped, with no SYN-ACK and no seed drawn. No UDP, ICMP or raw sockets, no echo reply, no IPv6.
> - **listen accepting from self:** the listener is bound to the interface address, so SYNs to broadcast don't match.
> - **Deviation (1), the gateway exemption, is safe.** Outbound to the gateway is refused (on QEMU, 10.0.2.0/24 is in self=), so the box can produce an inbound-from-gateway connection only through an outside hairpin, which is the stated residual. The gateway is where hostfwd connections arrive from.
> 
> **P2-1: the martian drop is not complete.** classify() drops martian sources only when next_header is TCP. Any other IPv4 (UDP, since socket-udp is off, or an unknown protocol) goes to the main interface, which answers with an ICMP 'protocol unreachable' (smoltcp ipv4.rs:240-248, icmpv4_reply) to the spoofed source. A throwaway test fed UDP and protocol 99 frames to ADDR from each source:
> - from ipd's own address: ipd **ARPs for its own address**, and the fake's check_frame panics ('ipd asked ARP for its own');
> - from 127.0.0.1: ARP for the gateway, then an ICMP to 127.0.0.1 through the gateway, which on a warm cache is a non-TCP IPv4 packet to the self set leaving the guest;
> - from a LAN host: an ICMP reply, which is 1:1 reflection for any spoofed victim.
> This breaks the frame invariant the bench's pcap check and the fake's check_frame assert: TCP only, no ARP for self. Fix in classify: drop every IPv4 packet that isn't TCP (ipd serves only TCP), and apply the martian test before the protocol test. Add UDP, ICMP and unknown-protocol frames from self-set sources to the stack tests and to the frames fuzz generator. That generator today only makes checksummed TCP or raw junk that never passes the IPv4 checksum, which is why 300 s of fuzzing couldn't find this.
> 
> == ISN (a CSPRNG-seeded interface per connect and per SYN, no fallback): verified ==
> - random_seq_no is drawn at exactly two sites: connect (tcp.rs:1063), which passes `fresh.context()` with an explicit local address, and Listen+SYN (tcp.rs:1919).
> - classify sends every SYN-without-ACK to ipd's address on a listened port through `fresh`. A SYN reaches the main interface only when it can't meet a LISTEN socket: a wrong destination, a fragment (refused, above), a port nobody listens on (an RST, no ISN), or a SynSent socket in simultaneous open (keeps its own ISN).
> - With no seed: connect answers unreachable, and a SYN is dropped. isn.rs checks every open's ISN against its seed and against the main PRNG's first 10k outputs.
> - Mutants caught: SYNs through main, and connect with main's context.
> - Cost per open: one `random` syscall plus one Interface::new (heapless inline tables, no sockets).
> - P3: when the backlog is full, fresh answers a SYN with an RST, which with an empty neighbour cache becomes an ARP broadcast. Under a SYN flood that is one ARP per SYN; state it.
> 
> == Grant, labelled refusal, visibility ==
> - **Narrowing:** Connect within Connect needs prefix len >= held and contained, and ports within. Listen within Listen only. Decode is canonical: host bits zero, lo <= hi, listen with addr 0 and len 0, at most 8 rules. Mutants caught: narrows=true, listen under connect, covers without the len check, ports without hi.
> - **Grant path:** scope_of(caller), then narrows, then add_scope, then mint_rooted, then unmint and collect_scopes unless the reply's handle was accepted (answer 168). Grants start a new port group, while new_connection children share their parent's.
> - **Labelled:** refused before decode on every call (9P gives Rerror PERMISSION, typed gives not_permitted), with handles closed and no bucket opened (tested). On sends, frames count only from the unlabelled ingress badge; every send's handles are closed and its transfer dropped.
> - **Visibility:** attach works only for root badges with a scope (the ingress badge can't). walk, open, read, write and stat go through check_socket for (badge, AdmitKey). /tcp lists only the owner's numbers, which are per owner and lowest free. Mutants caught: walk without check_socket, attach for any badge, the port-group rule, a grant in the same group.
> - **Deviation (2), each parked call served at most once per round:** sound, and needed. Without it a re-parked call would be resumed again in the same loop, so the round would never end. The current-call rule holds: poll runs only after a receive that returned no call; expire() clearing the tracker is harmless because nothing polls before the next receive; and on_call/serve run socket ops with the caller current, which is the right blame.
> 
> **P2-3: test gaps on key checks.** These planted bugs survived all 43 tests:
> - (a) on_send accepting frames from **any** unlabelled badge. That would let any client with an ipd handle inject arbitrary 'LAN' frames: forged RSTs into other users' connections, spoofed inbound connections to sshd. The code is right, but nothing tests it.
> - (b) on_send dropping the labels check on the ingress badge.
> - (c) ephemeral-port uniqueness removed (P2-8: a duplicate tuple mixes users' segments).
> - (d) the answer-168 undo in serve_own removed (only rt-level tests exist).
> - (e) the explicit half-open relisten removed. This one is equivalent, because smoltcp's 3 s timeout moves the socket to Closed and the Closed path relistens.
> Add tests for (a) to (d).
> 
> == Caps, sizing, SYN floods ==
> **P2-2: sockets don't follow the admission rules they claim (lib.rs guarantee 3).**
> - (a) sizing.rs max_sockets = sum(l.sockets) + rest x DEFAULT_SOCKETS repeats the in-flight flaw from review 3: an override below the default (the milestone steward's sockets=0) can be idle while a default bucket takes its slot. The true worst case is sum(max(l.sockets, default)) + rest x default: milestone 60, not 52. max_sockets is also the hard global cap in room(), so memory stays bounded, but a bucket under its own cap can then be refused by the global cap because of other buckets' sockets, which is a cross-bucket denial.
> - (b) The same happens through lingering: a disconnected connection's sockets stay charged to its AdmitKey for up to 70 s, but the admission bucket slot can be freed (no fids or state), so a newcomer's bucket takes the slot while those sockets still count against max_sockets.
> - (c) There is no fair share per badge for sockets: room() checks only the bucket's cap, so an agent sharing its sponsor's account can take all 8 sockets and lock the sponsor out (answer 90; CONTAINMENT). Fids, state and parked calls do get shares.
> Fix: charge sockets through Admission, for example as a resource or as State units, so they take buckets, shares and the worst-case sizing from the shared library, and keep the bucket alive while they linger. Otherwise apply max(cap, default) and a share rule in ipd.
> 
> SYN flood handling is otherwise right: backlog 1-8, half-open 3 s, then relisten, without failing the holder's read. Caps: room() uses the bucket cap (mutant caught).
> 
> == Supply chain ==
> - **heapless reading:** checked against the source: vec/mod.rs has 42 unsafe lines, linear_map.rs has 6, all in OccupiedEntry. insert and remove are safe code over Vec's iter, push and swap_remove. smoltcp calls new, get, insert, remove and iter, and the three containers hold Copy data. The reading is accurate, so the ratchet exclusion is justified.
> - **Miri:** not run. cargo-miri isn't installed for nightly, and I didn't install it (a toolchain change). It is a stated gap; it could be run in review whenever it is installed.
> - **build.rs guard works:** SMOLTCP_IFACE_NEIGHBOR_CACHE_COUNT=4 fails the build with the named variable.
> - rv64 and rv32 release builds pass.
> 
> == Fuzz (my spot runs, cargo +nightly fuzz) ==
> - session: 63,674 runs in 151 s, 2,122 new units, 415 MB RSS, no crash.
> - frames: 40,315 runs in 91 s, 864 new units, 464 MB RSS, no crash.
> See P2-1 for why frames can't reach the non-TCP case.
> 
> == P3 ==
> - ScopeId is a u32 incremented with `+= 1`, which panics or wraps after 2^32 grants. Use u64 or a checked add.
> - The ICMP reflection is closed by P2-1's fix.
> 
> Scope: servers/ipd, vendor/README, docs/NAMESPACES, Cargo files and test cases. No change to kernel/, model/ or K5 paths.

> P2-1: the martian drop is incomplete. classify() drops martian sources only for TCP, so UDP, ICMP or unknown-protocol IPv4 reaches the main interface, which replies with ICMP protocol-unreachable. From ipd's own address that makes ipd ARP for itself; from 127.0.0.1 a non-TCP packet goes to the self set; from a LAN host it's 1:1 reflection. Fix: in classify, apply the martian test BEFORE the protocol test, and drop every non-TCP IPv4 packet (ipd serves only TCP). Re-run frames fuzz for 5 minutes.
> P2-2 (my ruling on the fix): sockets bypass the admission rules. Charge sockets through the shared Admission as State units (an existing resource, so no new libs/rt API), so they get buckets, shares and the worst-case sizing from the library, and keep the bucket alive while its sockets linger. Recompute sizing with max(cap, default). Test the sponsor/agent share and the lingering case.
> P2-3: add tests that fail when planted: (a) on_send accepting frames from any unlabelled badge (it must accept only the ingress badge, or a client could inject forged RSTs or spoofed inbound connections); (b) on_send without the labels check on the ingress badge; (c) ephemeral ports not unique; (d) serve_own's answer-168 undo removed.
> P3s: state the one-ARP-per-SYN behaviour under a SYN flood with a full backlog; ScopeId as u64 or a checked add.
